decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already locks the entire approved Hero V and requires it to remain unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change, which fully covers preservation of its terminal treatment.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records the approved second V as a locked asset that must be carried forward unchanged, including its terminal geometry.
The existing same-message MODIFY already locks the approved É accent and prohibits redrawing or reinterpretation unless the client explicitly requests a change.
The existing same-message MODIFY already requires E and L exploration to occur around the locked Hero V, second V, and É accent while carrying those assets forward unchanged.
Locking the second V glyph and shared terminal treatment does not change its already-established relative-height hierarchy; the source does not specify a new hierarchy value.
The asset-lock decision preserves but does not modify the existing requirement that the Hero V and É accent peaks align on the same horizontal line.
Preserving the three locked glyph assets does not necessarily alter the current kerning, spacing, or unified-reading requirements.
The source decision concerns preservation of approved glyph assets and does not change the requirement to explain design rationale with review rounds.
Locking the shared terminal treatment and glyph assets does not change the deferred champagne material treatment or its role.
